artiest/dave-grohl.text:
David Eric Grohl was born in 1969 in Warren, Ohio, and grew up in Springfield, Virginia. His parents separated when he was seven. He taught himself to play guitar and, at thirteen, in Chicago, fell under the spell of punk. At first he listened to music that was harder, faster and darker, while his sister listened to new wave. In 1986, at seventeen, he joined the punk band Scream as drummer. When that group broke up in 1990, he became the drummer of Nirvana, with whom he became famous. He first played on Nevermind in 1991.

After Kurt Cobain's suicide in 1994, Nirvana ceased to exist. Grohl founded Foo Fighters as a one-man project. The album Foo Fighters appeared in 1995. He then put together a full band, and twelve studio albums have appeared since. He is also the drummer and a co-founder of the supergroup Them Crooked Vultures and has played with Queens of the Stone Age and Tenacious D. His side projects are Late!, with the album Pocketwatch, and Probot.

From 1997 Grohl directed the Foo Fighters' videos, and he made the documentaries Sound City in 2013, the series Sonic Highways in 2014 and What Drives Us in 2021. In 2021 his autobiography The Storyteller appeared. In 2014 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Nirvana and in 2021 with Foo Fighters. In 2016 Rolling Stone placed him twenty-seventh among the greatest drummers of all time.
artiest/dave-grohl.listen: Listen to Smells Like Teen Spirit by Nirvana and notice the drumming. Can you hear how the drums keep the song moving?

artiest/dave-holland.text: The bassist Dave Holland grew up in Wolverhampton and played in London, where Miles Davis heard him in 1968 and brought him to New York. Holland played during Miles's transition to electric music, on In a Silent Way and Bitches Brew. He then played in Circle with Chick Corea and Anthony Braxton, and recorded Conference of the Birds (1972) for ECM, with the saxophonists Anthony Braxton and Sam Rivers. Later he led a quintet and a big band that became known for their complex yet swinging compositions in unusual time signatures.
artiest/dave-holland.listen: Hear how the bass leads the group in an odd time signature.

artiest/dave-king.text:
David King is an American drummer from Minneapolis, born in 1970. He is a co-founder of the jazz groups The Bad Plus, with Reid Anderson, and Happy Apple, with Michael Lewis and Erik Fratzke. He also plays in the free jazz collective Buffalo Collision, with Tim Berne and Hank Roberts, in the electronic art pop project Halloween, Alaska and in The Gang Font, a noise and prog band with Greg Norton, the former bassist of Hüsker Dü. He also has a quintet of his own, the Dave King Trucking Company.

King has played or recorded with many names from modern jazz, including Bill Frisell, Joshua Redman, Joe Lovano, Dewey Redman, Kurt Rosenwinkel and Craig Taborn. He has also worked with people from other genres, such as the hip hop group Atmosphere, Jeff Beck and Meat Beat Manifesto. He wrote and played for modern dance with the Mark Morris Dance Group, for Isaac Mizrahi's fashion shows in New York and for the short animated films Bike Ride Story and Bike Race. In March 2008 he played his composition Thriftstore Jewelry with The Bad Plus on the TV show Late Night with Conan O'Brien.

As a solo artist he made, among other things, Indelicate in 2010 for the label Sunnyside, on which he plays duets with himself on piano and drums by means of overdubs. I'll Be Ringing You followed in 2012, with Bill Carrothers and Billy Peterson, and three albums with his Trucking Co.: Good Old Light, Adopted Highway and Surrounded By The Night. The documentary King for Two Days shows a two-day concert at the Walker Art Center. King shows how a drummer can move between jazz, rock and noise.
artiest/dave-king.listen: Listen to Thriftstore Jewelry by The Bad Plus and notice King's drumming. Can you hear how the drums think along with the piano and the bass, instead of just keeping time?

artiest/dave-liebman.text:
David Liebman was born in 1946 in Brooklyn. He is an American saxophonist, flautist, bandleader, composer and jazz educator, best known for his work on soprano saxophone. He contracted polio as a child, in 1949. From the age of nine he studied classical piano and from twelve, saxophone. Hearing John Coltrane in New York clubs such as Birdland, the Village Vanguard and the Half Note was decisive. He studied with Joe Allard, Lennie Tristano and Charles Lloyd and took a degree in American history at New York University.

In the early 1970s he helped set up the musicians' collective Free Life Communication, a hub of the New York loft jazz scene. He then played in the group of the drummer Elvin Jones. In 1973 he became a member of Miles Davis's ensemble in its electric period, and he can be heard on the live album Dark Magus and on the double album Get Up with It. He also appeared on On the Corner. At the same time he began groups of his own, first the Open Sky Trio and then Lookout Farm with the pianist Richie Beirach. The debut Lookout Farm appeared in 1974 on ECM. In 1981 he formed the group Quest with Beirach. With Michael Brecker, Joe Lovano and later Ravi Coltrane he led Saxophone Summit.

Liebman has played on more than five hundred recordings, about two hundred of them as leader. His work ranges from straight-ahead jazz through fusion and avant-garde to chamber music, with projects on Monk, Coltrane, Kurt Weill, Cole Porter, Jobim, Puccini and the Beatles. In 2011 he became an NEA Jazz Master. He founded and runs the International Association of Schools of Jazz. In this way he is both a performer and a teacher of jazz.
artiest/dave-liebman.listen: Listen to Lookout Farm from 1974 and notice the interplay between Liebman's saxophone and Richie Beirach's piano. Who leads and who follows?

artiest/dave-nada.text:
Dave Nada, real name David Villegas, is an American-Ecuadorian DJ and producer. He is credited as the inventor of moombahton, a fusion genre of house and reggaeton. He comes from College Park, Maryland, and began as a radio DJ for the University of Maryland's student station 88.1 WMUC. That aroused his interest in producing and DJing. In the early 2000s he got to know Jesse Tittsworth through a mutual friend, who invited him to play at his party Crunk in Washington. Later he organized TaxLo in Baltimore.

In 2007 Tittsworth introduced him to Matt Nordstrom. Together they formed the DJ and production duo Nadastrom, which shaped his career for about ten years. His sets and productions combine, among other things, electro, house, Baltimore club, punk, hip hop and Latin and folk influences. Nadastrom collaborated with and made remixes for, among others, Diplo, Skrillex, Dillon Francis, Celia Cruz, Kanye West and Steve Aoki.

Moombahton came about in November 2009. At a house party of high-school students he slowed the Afrojack remix of Moombah by Chuckie and Silvio Ecomo down to 108 beats per minute, so that it fitted better with the slower reggaeton and bachata that was being played there. The young crowd responded enthusiastically. At home he made more slowed-down edits of Dutch house tracks, shared them with other DJs and gave the sound the name moombahton, a blend of Moombah and reggaeton. Together with the DJ Sabo, Nadastrom started the party series Moombahton Massive. Nada also founded the label Hermanito with Tittsworth. His origin story shows how an accidental change of tempo can create a genre.
artiest/dave-nada.listen: Listen to Brazzer's Theme by Dillon Francis and Dave Nada and notice the tempo, which is slower than in ordinary house. Can you hear how the bass and the rhythm get more room as a result?

artiest/dave-rowntree.text:
Dave Rowntree is an English drummer, born in 1964 in Colchester. His mother played the viola and his father was a sound engineer at the BBC. At weekends he had percussion lessons at a music school, and with his father he played in a brass band. After school he studied computer science and worked as a programmer for Colchester council. In his youth he was already playing in bands with Graham Coxon.

In 1989 Coxon introduced him to Damon Albarn, who was starting a band in London. Rowntree quit his job and moved to London. With the bassist Alex James joining, and after two changes of name, it became Blur. The band signed to Food Records and in the 1990s grew into one of the great Britpop groups, with albums such as Modern Life Is Rubbish and Parklife. Rowntree provided the tight, energetic drumming beneath Albarn's clever, ironic songs.

Besides Blur, Rowntree did a remarkable number of other things. With Alex James he supported the British Mars lander Beagle 2, which carried a Blur-composed call sign. He ran an animation company, became a criminal-law solicitor and was active for the Labour Party, including as a councillor in Norfolk. He also composed music for television, such as for the series The Capture, and presented radio. In 2023 his first solo album, Radio Songs, appeared.
artiest/dave-rowntree.listen: Listen to Parklife by Blur. Notice Dave Rowntree's drums: a straightforward, driving rhythm that holds the half-spoken verses and the singalong chorus together.

artiest/dave-stewart.text:
Dave Stewart is an English musician, songwriter and producer, born in 1952 in Sunderland. As a teenager he already had a record contract with the folk rock band Longdancer, on Elton John's label, but success failed to come. He then lived for years in squats in London. At the end of 1976 he met the singer Annie Lennox, with whom he also began a relationship. Together they played in The Tourists, who had a hit in 1979 with I Only Want to Be with You.

In 1980 The Tourists broke up, and the relationship between Stewart and Lennox also ended. Even so, they continued to work together, as the duo Eurythmics. Stewart wrote the songs with Lennox and produced all the albums. Their big breakthrough came in 1983 with Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This), with a drum machine and a dark synthesizer line. Many more hits followed, until the duo stopped in 1990. They later came together a few more times.

Stewart also became a much-requested producer and writer for others, such as Tom Petty, Mick Jagger, Stevie Nicks and Ringo Starr. In the Netherlands he scored a number 1 hit with the saxophonist Candy Dulfer, Lily Was Here, made for the film De kassière. He won the Brit Award for best British producer three times. In 2022 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Lennox.
artiest/dave-stewart.listen: Listen to Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This) by Eurythmics. Notice the drum machine and Dave Stewart's single, constantly repeated synthesizer line in a minor key, above which Annie Lennox's cool voice sounds.

artiest/dave-tarras.text: Dave Tarras was born around 1895 in Teplyk in Ukraine and emigrated to New York in 1921. There he became the most sought-after clarinettist for Jewish weddings, radio and records, with an estimated 500 recordings. His playing was elegant and restrained, the opposite of that of Naftule Brandwein, and he made the bulgar rhythm popular. When the klezmer revival began, he taught young musicians such as Andy Statman.
artiest/dave-tarras.listen: Listen to Hopkele from 1928 and compare it with Brandwein: Tarras ornaments just as richly, but his tone stays round and his rhythm tight.

artiest/dave-tarras-en-sam-musiker.text:
Dave Tarras and Sam Musiker were father-in-law and son-in-law, and together they represent an important step in the history of klezmer. In the 1920s Tarras brought the musical traditions of the Old World to New York. Sam Musiker, born in New York in 1916, was a clarinettist and saxophonist and worked in both jazz and klezmer. He played in bars, restaurants and studios among jazz and swing musicians, and just as much at weddings and in hotels in Jewish musical life.

From 1938 Musiker played in Gene Krupa's orchestra, until it broke up in 1944, and could be heard on most of that band's records. He also played with Glenn Miller and with Sarah Vaughan and wrote arrangements for NBC. In klezmer he often worked with his brother Ray Musiker and with Tarras. In 1955 he led the album Tanz for Columbia, on which Tarras and Ray Musiker also played. It includes The Roumanian Fantasy.

Musiker brought elements of jazz and swing into klezmer and so created a New York sound of his own. His arrangements sound busy and driving: the drummer provides accents, the bass holds the pulse and piano or accordion plays the chords on the off-beat. He often used accordion to make a small band sound full. His brother Ray later passed that experience on to the klezmer revival.
artiest/dave-tarras-en-sam-musiker.listen: Listen to The Roumanian Fantasy and notice the clarinet, which can sob, laugh and shout. Can you hear how the rhythm section underneath keeps driving on while the clarinet plays freely?

artiest/dave-van-ronk.text:
Dave Van Ronk was an American folk singer and guitarist, born in 1936 in Brooklyn, New York. He began as a banjo player in traditional jazz bands, but when he discovered the blues of Reverend Gary Davis, Furry Lewis and Mississippi John Hurt in record shops, he took a different path. Around 1958 he accompanied himself on acoustic guitar and sang blues, folk and jazz. In Greenwich Village he became such a central figure that he was called the Mayor of MacDougal Street.

Van Ronk wrote few songs of his own. His strength lay in arranging old songs, from English ballads to blues, gospel and swing. He played ragtime on solo guitar, such as Scott Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag, and used the guitar like a piano, following the example of Gary Davis. To this he added rich harmonies that he picked up from Jelly Roll Morton and Duke Ellington. His voice could growl and whisper. Albums such as Folksinger (1962) and Just Dave Van Ronk (1964) show that style.

For young musicians he was a host and teacher. Bob Dylan often slept on his couch and put Van Ronk's arrangement of House of the Rising Sun on his first album. The Animals made a hit of it in 1964, and so a folk guitarist from the Village helped get folk rock going. Van Ronk died in 2002. The Coen brothers' film Inside Llewyn Davis is loosely based on his life.
artiest/dave-van-ronk.listen: Listen to House of the Rising Sun and follow the bass line on the guitar, which walks down step by step. Then compare his version with that of The Animals.

artiest/david-arnold.text: David Arnold from Luton began with music for student films by the director Danny Cannon. He wrote his first big film scores for Roland Emmerich: Stargate (1994) and Independence Day (1996), with large orchestra, choir and heroic brass themes. In 1997 he made the album Shaken and Stirred, with new versions of Bond songs by pop artists. He was then asked to write Tomorrow Never Dies (1997). He became the Bond composer of his generation and wrote five Bond films, up to Quantum of Solace (2008). Arnold blends John Barry's brass sound with electronic beats. With Michael Price he wrote the music for the TV series Sherlock (2010).
artiest/david-arnold.listen: Notice the Barry-like brass and the jazz chords, supplemented with modern electronic rhythms.

artiest/david-bowie.text:
David Bowie was born David Robert Jones in 1947 in Brixton, a district of London. He showed that a rock star could play a role, and that an artist could keep reinventing himself. From glam rock through soul and electronic music to dance music: every few years he sounded different.

His first big hit was Space Oddity, released in July 1969, five days before the launch of Apollo 11. The breakthrough came with The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars (1972). Bowie invented a rock star from space and became that character, on stage and off, with the guitarist Mick Ronson and the Spiders from Mars as his band. A performance of Starman on Top of the Pops in July 1972 made him known in England. On 3 July 1973 he said farewell to Ziggy at the Hammersmith Odeon in London. On Young Americans (1975) he made what he called 'plastic soul', and Fame became his first number 1 hit in America. In West Berlin, with Brian Eno and the producer Tony Visconti, he made Low and "Heroes" (both 1977) and then Lodger (1979). Let's Dance (1983), with Nile Rodgers as co-producer, became his greatest commercial success.

The New Romantics danced to Bowie at the Blitz club in London, and regulars of that club appeared in the video for Ashes to Ashes (1980). With Major Tom (völlig losgelöst), Peter Schilling wrote a sequel to Space Oddity. Bowie died in New York in January 2016, two days after the release of his last album Blackstar.
artiest/david-bowie.listen: Ziggy Stardust opens with a guitar riff by Mick Ronson, with Bowie's acoustic twelve-string guitar beneath it. Listen to how that raw electric riff and the clear twelve-string together carry the whole song.

artiest/david-byrne.text:
David Byrne was born in 1952 in Dumbarton, Scotland. The family moved to Canada and then to Maryland in the United States, where his father was an electronics engineer. He played harmonica, guitar, accordion and violin from an early age, and his father converted a tape recorder for him so that he could make multitrack recordings. He studied briefly at the Rhode Island School of Design, where he met Chris Frantz.

In 1974 Byrne moved to New York. Frantz and his girlfriend Tina Weymouth followed, and Weymouth learned to play bass. In 1975 the band, Talking Heads, played its first gig. Jerry Harrison joined later. Talking Heads became one of the important groups of new wave, with songs such as Psycho Killer, Life During Wartime, Burning Down the House and a version of Take Me to the River. The music was nervous and angular, with influences from funk and African rhythms. Byrne often sang in a jerky, strange way, like an outsider observing the world. In 1991 the band stopped.

Byrne worked a great deal with Brian Eno. Their 1981 album My Life in the Bush of Ghosts used samples and found sounds at an early date. As a solo artist he made, among other things, Rei Momo, full of Latin American dance styles, and American Utopia. He founded the label Luaka Bop and made films, opera, theatre and visual art. Among other honours he received an Oscar, for the music of The Last Emperor.
artiest/david-byrne.listen: Listen to Once in a Lifetime by Talking Heads. Notice the funky, repeating groove and the way Byrne delivers the verses almost like a sermon.

artiest/david-cassidy.text:
David Cassidy was born in 1950 in New York, the son of the actor and singer Jack Cassidy and the actress Evelyn Ward. His parents were often on tour, and for the first few years he grew up with his grandparents in New Jersey. His father later married the singer and actress Shirley Jones. In 1969 David made his Broadway debut and signed with Universal, after which he got small roles in television series.

In 1970 he was cast as Keith Partridge in The Partridge Family, a television series about a singing family. Shirley Jones played his mother. When it turned out that he could sing well, he was allowed to do the lead vocals on the records. The music was played by studio musicians. The first single, I Think I Love You, became a big hit. Cassidy himself later called the music bubblegum: light, cheerful pop for teenagers.

The series made him an enormous teen idol. For a while he was the best-paid performer in the world, and his fan club was bigger than that of The Beatles or Elvis. As a solo artist he scored with Cherish, How Can I Be Sure and Could It Be Forever, especially in England. But Cassidy felt trapped in the image of an idol. He wanted to be a serious rock musician, like Mick Jagger. In this way he became an example of a star made by television and marketing. He died in 2017.
artiest/david-cassidy.listen: Listen to I Think I Love You by The Partridge Family. Notice the tight, glossy studio accompaniment and the backing vocals, and Cassidy's voice, which puts the teenage crush front and centre.

artiest/david-gilmour.text:
David Gilmour was born in 1946 in Cambridge. There, at school, he got to know Syd Barrett and Roger Waters, the two boys who would later play in Pink Floyd. Gilmour taught himself to play guitar from a book and a record by Pete Seeger and, as a teenager, played in the blues rock band Jokers Wild. In 1967 he travelled to France with a group of his own, but it came to little. At the end of that year Pink Floyd asked him to join, because Barrett, owing to mental health problems, was functioning less and less well. Shortly afterwards Barrett left the group.

As lead guitarist and singer, Gilmour gave the sound of Pink Floyd a new direction. When Roger Waters left in 1985, he took over the leadership. Under his leadership the albums A Momentary Lapse of Reason in 1987, The Division Bell in 1994 and The Endless River in 2014 appeared. He also made five solo albums: David Gilmour in 1978, About Face in 1984, On an Island in 2006, Rattle That Lock in 2015 and Luck and Strange in 2024. His wife, the writer Polly Samson, co-wrote many of his lyrics.

Gilmour plays guitar with a great feeling for tone: long, singing notes instead of fast runs. That made him one of the best-known guitarists in rock history. He also helped others on their way. He paid for Kate Bush's first recordings and helped her get a record contract. In the course he appears in the story about Wish You Were Here, where the sound of a radio comes from his car.
artiest/david-gilmour.listen: Listen to a Pink Floyd song featuring Gilmour, such as Wish You Were Here, and notice his guitar. Can you hear how he lets a long note sing and fade away?

artiest/david-guetta.text:
Pierre David Guetta was born in 1967 in Paris, where he also grew up. He is a French DJ and producer. His father was a sociologist from a Moroccan-Jewish family, and his mother was of Belgian descent. His debut album Just a Little More Love appeared in 2002. Guetta Blaster followed in 2004 and Pop Life in 2007. More than once he was voted the world's best DJ in the DJ Mag polls, including in 2011 and 2020.

His breakthrough to the general public came with the fourth album One Love in 2009. It included When Love Takes Over with Kelly Rowland, Gettin' Over You, Sexy Bitch with Akon and Memories with Kid Cudi. The first three reached number one in England. The fifth album Nothing but the Beat from 2011 had hits such as Where Them Girls At, Without You with Usher, Titanium with Sia and Turn Me On with Nicki Minaj. In 2018 came 7, with twelve tracks under his alias Jack Back. In 2022 he released I'm Good (Blue) with Bebe Rexha.

Guetta combines dance music with singers from pop and hip hop. In 2019, together with the producer Morten Breum, he came up with the subgenre future rave. In 2021 he sold his music catalogue. He won two Grammys. In 2013 Billboard ranked When Love Takes Over among the best dance-pop collaborations of all time. His work shows how electronic dance music gained a permanent place in pop music in the 2000s.
artiest/david-guetta.listen: Listen to Titanium with Sia and notice how Sia's voice and the electronic sounds together carry the chorus. Which of the two feels like the lead?

artiest/david-hasselhoff.text:
David Michael Hasselhoff, nicknamed the Hoff, was born in 1952 in Baltimore. He is an American actor, singer and television personality. He became known through the soap opera The Young and the Restless, in which he played Dr Snapper Foster from 1975 to 1982. Knight Rider followed, in which he played Michael Knight, and from 1989 Baywatch, in which he was the lifeguard Mitch Buchannon. He also produced Baywatch himself. His great dream was a career on Broadway. In 2000 he made his debut there in the musical Jekyll & Hyde.

As a singer he made fifteen studio albums, which were successful above all in the German-speaking part of Europe, where he received several gold and platinum records. His song Looking for Freedom reached number one in Germany and Switzerland. The albums Night Rocker appeared in 1985, Lovin' Feelings in 1987, Looking for Freedom in 1989 and Crazy for You in 1990. Later came, among others, Du in 1994, Hooked on a Feeling in 1997, Sings America in 2004 and 30 in 2017.

In the 2000s he was a judge on TV talent shows such as America's Got Talent from 2006 to 2009 and Britain's Got Talent in 2011. He also acted in films, including DodgeBall, The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie and Click, and in 1998 was the first actor to play Marvel's Nick Fury, in a TV film. His musical career is an example of an actor whose popularity, through television, gained a second life in pop music, especially in Germany.
artiest/david-hasselhoff.listen: Listen to Looking for Freedom and notice the sung melody and the chorus. Can you hear how his voice and the accompaniment form a simple, singalong song?

artiest/david-hill.text:
David Hill is an English choral conductor and organist. He was born in 1957 in Carlisle and was educated at Chetham's School of Music in Manchester and at St John's College, Cambridge, where he was an organ scholar under George Guest. As a boy he already appeared in an episode of Coronation Street from 1970, in which he broke into a church to play the organ.

His career revolved around the English cathedral choirs. From 1980 he was for two years sub-organist of Durham Cathedral. He then directed the music at Westminster Cathedral, from 1982 to 1987, and at Winchester Cathedral, from 1987 to 2002. In those years he recorded a great deal of choral music, from Renaissance music by Tallis and Christopher Tye to Mozart, Rachmaninov, Fauré and Carmina Burana. Later he returned to St John's College as director of music, was principal conductor of the BBC Singers from 2007 to 2017 and led The Bach Choir in London. Since 2013 he has also worked in the United States as professor of choral conducting and conductor of the Yale Schola Cantorum.

The sound he strives for is that of the English cathedral choir: clear boys' voices and men's voices, sung in tune in a resonant space. His recordings show how broad that repertoire is and how strongly the choral tradition of the English church still resonates in the classical world. In 2019 the British Queen appointed him a Member of the Order of the British Empire for his services to music.
artiest/david-hill.listen: Listen to one of the choral works on his album Spem in alium. Can you hear how the voices weave through one another like separate layers and yet form a single sound?

artiest/david-lee-roth.text:
David Lee Roth was born in 1954 in Bloomington, Indiana, and grew up in Pasadena, California. He sang in local bands before becoming the singer of Van Halen in the 1970s. With that hard rock band he played the clubs of Los Angeles, until the group got a record contract after a demo that Gene Simmons of Kiss helped to record. The debut album Van Halen appeared in 1978 and made the band nationally known at once.

Roth was the face of the group. He wore tight trousers, leapt high into the air and wrote the lyrics about parties, dancing and women. In doing so he stood opposed to Eddie Van Halen, who wanted to make darker and deeper music, including with synthesizers. After the album 1984 the band broke up. In 1985 Roth released, as his first work of his own, the EP Crazy from the Heat, with striking pop hits from an older tradition. The solo albums Eat 'Em and Smile in 1986 and Skyscraper in 1988 followed, with the hit Just Like Paradise. For these he worked with top musicians such as Steve Vai and Billy Sheehan. Later albums such as A Little Ain't Enough and Your Filthy Little Mouth were less successful. He returned to Van Halen a few more times, including in 2007.

His nickname is Diamond Dave. Roth showed that a hard rock singer can also be a showman and an entertainer. That role influenced many later frontmen in rock.
artiest/david-lee-roth.listen: Listen to Just Like Paradise and notice how Roth sings: more like a showman than a screaming rock singer. Can you hear how the synthesizers make the sound more pop?

artiest/david-mancuso.text:
David Mancuso was an American DJ, born in 1944 in Utica, New York. He spent his first five years in an orphanage and later often ran away from home. As a teenager he fell under the spell of rhythm and blues. At sixteen he left school and worked as a dishwasher to save for a move to New York, where he arrived in 1962. There he went to rent parties in Harlem and the hippie clubs of the East Village.

From 1966 he played records for friends in his home. On 14 February 1970 he held his first big party at 647 Broadway, Love Saves the Day. From it grew The Loft: a private, invitation-only party, and not an ordinary commercial nightclub. Mancuso sold no food or drink to the public and therefore, after a long process, did not need a licence. He also helped set up the system through which DJs received promotional records.

The Loft became the model for many later clubs in New York, such as the Paradise Garage, The Gallery and The Saint. In this way Mancuso played a key role in the emergence of the dance music culture of the 1970s, in which the DJ and the dance floor came to take centre stage. He created a party where people danced together to music that was carefully chosen. Later he founded a label for carefully mastered dance music. He died in 2016.
artiest/david-mancuso.listen: Listen to a track from the compilation series David Mancuso Presents The Loft. Notice the long, continuous dance rhythm and how a track like this is made to keep a full dance floor moving for hours.

artiest/david-mason.text:
David Mason was an English trumpeter, born in 1926 in London. He studied at the Royal College of Music. Because during the Second World War he was still too young for conscription, while many older musicians had to serve, he already got a lot of work in London as a teenager. Later he played in the orchestra of the Royal Opera House, became principal trumpet of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra and played for a long time with the Philharmonia. For thirty years he taught at the Royal College of Music.

In the classical world he stood out in 1958, when he played the flugelhorn at the premiere of Ralph Vaughan Williams's Ninth Symphony, an instrument mainly known from jazz and brass bands. But his best-known notes sound in pop music. On 17 January 1967 he recorded the piccolo trumpet solo for The Beatles' Penny Lane at Abbey Road Studios. The idea grew out of a performance of Bach's Second Brandenburg Concerto, and the solo accordingly sounds like imitation Baroque.

The piccolo trumpet has a clear, high sound that stands out well above the rest of the music. The producer George Martin later wrote that nothing like it had ever been done in rock music. Mason also played on other Beatles songs, such as A Day in the Life, Magical Mystery Tour and All You Need Is Love. He died in 2011.
artiest/david-mason.listen: Listen to Penny Lane by The Beatles and wait for the solo in the middle. Notice David Mason's high, clear piccolo trumpet, which, with its quick, ornate runs, sounds like music from the time of Bach.

artiest/david-munrow.text:
David Munrow was a British musician and historian of early music. He was born in 1942 in Birmingham and studied English at Cambridge. There he began to play instruments from South America, which he had brought back after a year in Peru. Professor Thurston Dart encouraged him to investigate the connection between those folk instruments and the old European instruments. Munrow played bassoon and piano and sang, and taught himself to play a whole collection of medieval and Renaissance instruments.

Together with Christopher Hogwood he founded the Early Music Consort of London, a group of specialists who played on replica instruments. His great breakthrough came with the music for the television series The Six Wives of Henry VIII, which aroused worldwide interest in Renaissance music and instruments. He also wrote music for films, such as Ken Russell's The Devils in 1971 and Zardoz in 1974. On BBC Radio 3 he presented 655 episodes of the programme Pied Piper, which ranged from Monteverdi to the Electric Light Orchestra. He made more than fifty records, with an emphasis on the Middle Ages and the Renaissance.

Munrow died in 1976, at the age of 33, leaving behind a large collection of instruments. Probably no one in the second half of the twentieth century did more to make early music popular in Britain. A recording by his ensemble was chosen for the Voyager Golden Record, the gold disc that went into space.
artiest/david-munrow.listen: Listen to The Fairie Round as performed by his Early Music Consort, the piece that went into space with Voyager. Notice the dance character and the sound of the old instruments.

artiest/david-munrow-en-the-early-music-.text:
The Early Music Consort of London was a British ensemble of the late 1960s and the 1970s that played medieval and Renaissance music according to historical performance practice. The musicologists Christopher Hogwood and David Munrow founded it in 1967. Munrow was inspired by the Alte Musik movement in Germany and wanted to win over the British public to music of the Middle Ages and the Renaissance. He had studied with Hogwood at Pembroke College, Cambridge.

The group made many influential recordings. Titles include Ecco la primavera, on fourteenth-century Florentine music, from 1969, The Triumphs of Maximilian I and The Six Wives of Henry VIII from 1970, Music of the Crusades from 1971 and Music for Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain from 1972. In 1976 The Art of the Netherlands appeared as three LPs. One piece from the album Instruments of the Middle Ages and Renaissance, The Fairie Round by Anthony Holborne, was chosen by NASA for the Voyager Golden Record, which went into space in 1977 aboard Voyager 1 and 2.

The ensemble is seen as the driving force behind the British early music revival of the late twentieth century. It played the music on old instruments, in a sound that was new to many listeners. The group ceased to exist in 1976, after Munrow's death. In the course, the Consort shows how the work of the fourteenth-century poet and composer Machaut sounded.
artiest/david-munrow-en-the-early-music-.listen: Listen to Ma fin est mon commencement and notice the blend of the voices or instruments and the soft, calm movement of the lines. How does it sound that this song is so old?

artiest/david-newman.text:
David Newman is an American composer and conductor who became known mainly for his film music. He was born in 1954 in Los Angeles, the son of the Hollywood composer Alfred Newman. His brother Thomas, his sister Maria and his cousin Randy are also composers, so that Hollywood and film music naturally belonged to his childhood.

His first film work was, in 1984, Tim Burton's short film Frankenweenie. In 1987 he composed the music for Throw Momma from the Train, the start of a long collaboration with the director Danny DeVito, for whom he also scored The War of the Roses, Hoffa and Matilda. In the early years he wrote mainly music for B-movies, later mostly for comedies. For the animated film Anastasia from 1997 he received an Oscar nomination, after his father had earlier written the music for the 1956 live-action film. He also composed for Ice Age, Serenity and The Brave Little Toaster. In 1997 he re-recorded the 20th Century Fox fanfare, a piece his father had written.

Newman regularly conducts major orchestras, including the Los Angeles Philharmonic and, since 2012, the Vienna Radio Symphony Orchestra. His music shows how in Hollywood a family of composers passed on the orchestral film sound from generation to generation.
artiest/david-newman.listen: Listen to the 20th Century Fox fanfare in his 1997 recording. Notice how a few seconds of orchestra are enough to recognize an entire film studio.

artiest/david-paich.text:
David Paich is an American keyboard player, singer and songwriter. He was born in 1954, the son of the jazz composer and arranger Marty Paich, and so grew up with arranging work and studio music. In 1977 he founded the band Toto, of which he became the main songwriter and one of the keyboard players.

For Toto he wrote, with others, many of the best-known songs, such as Hold the Line from 1978, Rosanna and Africa. He also worked as a session musician, writer and producer. Together with Boz Scaggs he wrote Lowdown and Lido Shuffle for the album Silk Degrees from 1976. In 1977 he produced Aretha Franklin's song Break It to Me Gently. On Michael Jackson's album Thriller he played piano and synthesizer, and in the 1980s he often worked with the producers Quincy Jones and David Foster. In 2009 he was inducted into the Musicians Hall of Fame with the other members of Toto. In 2022 his first solo album Forgotten Toys appeared.

Paich shows how the sound of the Californian studio musicians shaped pop music around 1980. His songs remained radio hits long after the band had broken up.
artiest/david-paich.listen: Listen to Africa and notice the keyboards. Which sounds go with the chords, and what do the synthesizers do beneath the vocals?

artiest/david-porter.text:
David Porter is an American songwriter from Memphis. He was born in 1941, the ninth of twelve children, and began singing in church, often with his classmate Maurice White, who later founded Earth, Wind and Fire. Through Chips Moman he ended up at the label Satellite, which soon became Stax Records, Memphis's well-known soul label.

At Stax, Porter was the first staff songwriter. He brought artists such as The Emotions and The Soul Children to the label and brought in Isaac Hayes as a writing partner. Together Porter and Hayes wrote most of Sam & Dave's hits, including Soul Man and Hold On, I'm Comin'. Porter also made records of his own. In 1965 his single Can't See You When I Want To appeared, and in the early 1970s albums followed such as Gritty, Groovy, & Gettin' It and Victim of the Joke?, on which he recorded Help! by The Beatles. In 1978 he accompanied the brief return of the Stax label.

In 2005 Porter was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame. He wrote more than 1,700 songs for artists from Aretha Franklin to Wu-Tang Clan, and his songs were often sampled. In 2012 he founded the organization The Consortium MMT in Memphis, to train young musicians.
artiest/david-porter.listen: Listen to Soul Man by Sam & Dave. Notice how vocals, horns and rhythm keep answering one another, as Porter and Hayes wrote it for Stax.

artiest/david-raksin.text: David Raksin was born in 1912 in Philadelphia. He studied composition, with Arnold Schoenberg in Los Angeles among others. His first big job was working out Chaplin's melodies for Modern Times (1936). He became known through Otto Preminger's Laura (1944). Preminger first wanted to use Duke Ellington's Sophisticated Lady, but Raksin was given one weekend to write something else. That is how the Laura theme came about. Johnny Mercer later wrote lyrics for it and it became a jazz standard with hundreds of recordings. Raksin wrote more than a hundred film scores, including Forever Amber (1947) and The Bad and the Beautiful (1952). Later he taught at USC and UCLA.
artiest/david-raksin.listen: Notice how one long, searching melody with unexpected harmonic turns carries the whole film and keeps returning in a different colour.

artiest/david-sanborn.text: The alto saxophonist David Sanborn grew up in St. Louis and played the saxophone as a child to strengthen his lungs after polio. He played with blues musicians and, at Woodstock, in Paul Butterfield's band. As a studio musician he played on records by David Bowie, Stevie Wonder and James Taylor; his solo on Bowie's Young Americans became well known. From 1975 he made albums of his own. His tone is sharp, emotional and loud, with influences from rhythm and blues. That made him one of the best-known saxophonists in smooth jazz and pop. He also hosted the television programme Night Music. He died in 2024.
artiest/david-sanborn.listen: Hear the fierce, almost weeping tone of the alto saxophone.

artiest/david-shire.text: David Shire was born in 1937 in Buffalo and studied at Yale. At first he wrote mainly musicals, together with the lyricist Richard Maltby Jr. In the 1970s he became one of the composers of New Hollywood. For Francis Ford Coppola's The Conversation (1974) he wrote a score for solo piano, lonely and jazzy, like the eavesdropper in the film. In the same year, for The Taking of Pelham One Two Three, he made a funky score with brass and electric bass, built on twelve-tone rows. All the President's Men (1976), by contrast, has very little music. Later he won an Oscar for the song 'It Goes Like It Goes' from Norma Rae (1979). David Fincher asked him for Zodiac (2007).
artiest/david-shire.listen: In Pelham, notice the angular, dissonant brass lines above a funky bass line: twelve-tone technique sounds here like urban crime funk.

artiest/david-tudor.text:
David Tudor was an American pianist and composer of experimental music. He was born in 1926 in Philadelphia and began as an organist. Later he studied piano with Irma Wolpe and composition with Stefan Wolpe. In 1950 he gave the first performance in the United States of Pierre Boulez's second piano sonata. A European tour in 1954 strengthened his name as one of the most important interpreters of avant-garde music.

Composers wrote music for him, including Morton Feldman and above all John Cage. Karlheinz Stockhausen dedicated Klavierstück VI to him. From 1951 Tudor played almost all of Cage's indeterminate piano works, making choices himself about how the score sounded. From the early 1960s he played less piano and wrote mainly electronic works, often for the Merce Cunningham Dance Company. His self-built electronic circuits are regarded as milestones of live electronic music. After Cage's death in 1992 he became the company's musical director. In 1969 he founded the first electronic music studio in India, in Ahmedabad.

Tudor made the pianist a co-creator and showed that electronics could itself become an instrument.
artiest/david-tudor.listen: Listen to a recording of Microphone from 1978. Notice what you hear: is it a melody, or mainly sound?

artiest/david-zinman.text:
David Zinman is an American conductor. He was born in 1936 in New York and studied violin at Oberlin and theory and composition at the University of Minnesota. He learned conducting at Tanglewood and from Pierre Monteux, whose assistant he was from 1961 to 1964. His career took him through three countries. From 1965 to 1977 he was associate conductor of the Netherlands Chamber Orchestra and from 1979 to 1982 principal conductor of the Rotterdam Philharmonic Orchestra. In the United States he led the Rochester Philharmonic and the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra. In 1995 he became music director of the Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich.

In Zurich he devised new concert formats, such as the late-evening concerts Tonhalle Late, in which classical music was played in a nightclub atmosphere. He recorded all of Beethoven's symphonies for Arte Nova, following Jonathan Del Mar's new edition of the scores. He also conducted film music, such as the film of the New York City Ballet's Nutcracker from 1993.

His best-known record is the 1992 recording of Henryk Górecki's Symphony No. 3 with Dawn Upshaw and the London Sinfonietta. It became an international bestseller, unusual for contemporary classical music. Zinman received five Grammys, two Grand Prix du Disque and two Edison Awards for his recordings. He showed that a conductor can reach a large audience even outside the standard repertoire.
artiest/david-zinman.listen: Listen to his recording of Górecki's third symphony. Notice how slowly the music unfolds and how the soprano rises above the orchestra.

artiest/davido.text:
Davido, in full David Adedeji Adeleke, was born in 1992 in Atlanta and grew up in Lagos. His father is a Nigerian businessman. At sixteen Davido went to the United States to study business administration, bought music equipment there and made beats. Together with his cousins he formed the group KB International. He dropped out of his studies, worked on his voice in London and began professionally in music in March 2011. Later he did go on to study music at Babcock University.

His first album Omo Baba Olowo from 2011 mixes Afrobeats and hip hop. The single Dami Duro brought him fame. In 2016 he signed with Sony Music and RCA Records, founded his own label Davido Music Worldwide and released the EP Son of Mercy. The albums A Better Time in 2020, Timeless in 2023 and 5ive in 2025 followed. In 2019 New African magazine named him one of the hundred most influential Africans, and in 2021 he was on the Next List of the Time 100.

Davido's music stands for the new Nigerian pop music known as Afrobeats: danceable rhythms, singing in English and Yoruba and electronic beats with influences from hip hop and R&B. He is regarded as a cultural ambassador for Nigeria and speaks out on human rights in Africa. His songs show how popular music from Lagos is heard worldwide.
artiest/davido.listen: Listen to Fall and notice the relaxed, danceable rhythm and the melodic singing. Where do you hear influences of R&B and hip hop, and where those of African rhythms?

artiest/dawn-upshaw.text:
Dawn Upshaw is an American soprano. She was born in 1960 in Nashville and sings both opera and art song. Her repertoire runs from the Baroque to contemporary music, and that last is what makes her special. Many composers wrote for her, including Henri Dutilleux, Osvaldo Golijov and John Harbison.

Her name was established by the recordings of 1989 and 1991. For the album Knoxville: Summer of 1915, with works by Barber, Menotti, Harbison and Stravinsky, among others, she received a Grammy for Best Classical Vocal Soloist in 1989. In 1991 she won the same award for The Girl with Orange Lips, with songs by Falla and Ravel. She also recorded operas, such as Lucio Silla in 1990 and L'elisir d'amore. In 2003 she won a Grammy together with the Kronos Quartet for Berg's Lyric Suite, and in 2006 for the recording of Golijov's opera Ainadamar. She also sang the solo part in the recording of Henryk Górecki's third symphony under David Zinman.

In 2006 Upshaw founded the vocal arts programme for singers at Bard College, of which she was artistic director until 2019. She also directs the vocal programme of the Tanglewood Music Center. She showed that a classical singer can make contemporary music the core of her work.
artiest/dawn-upshaw.listen: Listen to a song from Knoxville: Summer of 1915. Notice how clearly she sings the text, as if she were telling a story.

artiest/de-dijk.text:
De Dijk was founded in 1981 by the brothers Huub and Hans van der Lubbe and the guitarist Nico Arzbach. The band emerged from the funk group Stampei from Krommenie and named itself after Amsterdam's Zeedijk. The first gig was on 1 October 1981 at Paradiso, supporting Raymond van het Groenewoud. For forty years De Dijk sang in Dutch about Amsterdam and the people who live there.

The music came from America: soul, blues and rhythm and blues, with horns and a tight rhythm section. The debut album De Dijk appeared in 1982. In 1987 came Wakker in een vreemde wereld, with Mag het licht uit on it, written by Huub van der Lubbe and Nico Arzbach. The band received the Zilveren Harp (Silver Harp), a Dutch music prize, that year. The album Niemand in de stad (1989) was their breakthrough and sold 100,000 copies. The Gouden Harp (Golden Harp) followed later (1993), and an Edison Oeuvreprijs, the Dutch lifetime achievement award (2005).

De Dijk remained one of the most popular live bands in the Netherlands. In 2010 the group made the album Hold On Tight with the American soul singer Solomon Burke. In 2005 De Dijk recorded a version of their own of Welterusten mijnheer de president by Boudewijn de Groot. The last studio album was Nu of Nou (2019). In May 2022 Huub van der Lubbe announced that he was stopping. The last concert was on 17 December 2022. The band's archive is going to the Amsterdam City Archives.
artiest/de-dijk.listen: Mag het licht uit is a love song in the form of an American soul ballad. Listen to how the band takes over the slow tempo of those ballads, while Huub van der Lubbe sings in plain, everyday Dutch.

artiest/de-jeugd-van-tegenwoordig.text:
De Jeugd van Tegenwoordig is a Dutch hip hop group from Amsterdam. The group consists of the producer Bas Bron and the rappers Vjèze Fur, Faberyayo and Willie Wartaal. It began as a project of Bron's, who wanted to make tracks with different rappers. When the word watskeburt became popular street slang in Amsterdam, Bron and Pepijn Lanen, Faberyayo, made a track about it, really only for friends. Freddie Tratlehner, Vjèze Fur, rapped along. Later Willie Wartaal joined too. The name comes from a T-shirt belonging to Lanen's brother.

In May 2005 Watskeburt?! appeared. At first little happened, but radio stations picked it up, and within a short time it was at number 1. The album Parels voor de zwijnen followed that same year. Next came, among others, De Machine, with Hollereer, and De lachende derde, with Sterrenstof. In interviews the members enjoyed telling made-up stories, for example that they had found the lyrics in the metro.

De Jeugd van Tegenwoordig turned language into a playground. The lyrics are full of puns, invented words and scraps of other languages, over beats with strong influences from electronic music. That was new in Dutch hip hop, which until then had often sounded more serious or harder. The group won an Edison, among other awards, and played at Lowlands, Pinkpop and Rock Werchter.
artiest/de-jeugd-van-tegenwoordig.listen: Listen to Watskeburt?!. Notice the electronic beat and how the rappers play with sound and words: it is less about a story than about the fun of language itself.

artiest/de-la-ghetto.text:
De La Ghetto is the stage name of Rafael Castillo Torres, an American singer and rapper who was born in 1984 in the Bronx in New York. His father was Dominican and his mother Puerto Rican. In 2004 he met Arcángel, who also came from New York, and together they formed the duo Arcángel & De la Ghetto. Their first single Ven, Pégate appeared in 2005 on Naldo's mixtape Sangre Nueva. He then signed to Zion's label Baby Records.

In 2006 he began a solo career. The following year two hits appeared, a remix of Siente el Boom by Tito el Bambino and Sensación del Bloque with Randy, which has since been viewed more than two hundred million times on YouTube. His first solo album Masacre musical came out in 2008. Later came Geezy Boyz: The Album in 2013, Mi movimiento in 2018 and Los chulitos in 2020. Mi movimiento was nominated for a Latin Grammy for Best Urban Album in 2019, and the song Caliente also received a nomination.

De La Ghetto's music combines reggaeton with hip hop and trap. In this way he is one of the artists who shaped Latin trap.
artiest/de-la-ghetto.listen: Listen to Caliente from Mi movimiento. Notice how the reggaeton rhythm is combined with rap and trap sounds.

artiest/de-la-soul.text:
De La Soul is a hip hop group from Amityville on Long Island, New York. Kelvin Mercer (Posdnuos), David Jolicoeur (Trugoy the Dove) and Vincent Mason (Maseo) met at secondary school. With a demo of Plug Tunin' they attracted the attention of the producer Prince Paul, and in 1989 their debut 3 Feet High and Rising appeared. It became their greatest success, with the hit Me Myself and I.

The album sounded different from most rap of the moment. The group stacked samples from all kinds of sources on top of one another, made funny interludes and rapped about peace and harmony. They called it the D.A.I.S.Y. Age, which stood for da inner sound, y'all. The public soon stuck the label hippies on them, and the members hated that. On De La Soul Is Dead (1991) the cover therefore shows a broken flowerpot with daisies. Buhloone Mindstate (1993) and Stakes Is High (1996) followed, among others, the title track of the latter produced by J Dilla.

De La Soul belonged to the Native Tongues, a circle of groups such as A Tribe Called Quest and the Jungle Brothers who shaped jazz rap and alternative hip hop. The free sampling also had a downside: The Turtles sued the group, and owing to problems with rights and contracts their music was not on streaming services until 2023. In 2006 they won a Grammy for Feel Good Inc. with Gorillaz. Trugoy died in 2023.
artiest/de-la-soul.listen: Listen to Me Myself and I and notice the cheerful, funky sample on which the raps rest. Hear how in the lyrics the group says that they just want to be themselves, and not the label that others stick on them.

artiest/de-spelbrekers.text:
De Spelbrekers were a Dutch vocal duo, consisting of Theo Rekkers and Huug Kok. They met during the Second World War in a munitions factory in Bremen, where they worked as forced labourers. In 1945, after the war, they formed the duo. Their recording career began in 1950 and in the 1950s they released many singles.

The greatest success of those years was Oh wat ben je mooi, which reached number five in the Dutch charts in 1956. In 1962 they won the national selection for the Eurovision Song Contest with Katinka and represented the Netherlands at the contest in Luxembourg. Katinka received no points at all there, but became a big hit all the same and remained an evergreen. After that they never managed to repeat that success. In the 1970s Kok and Rekkers moved into management and guided the careers of, among others, André van Duin, Ben Cramer and Saskia & Serge. In 1975 they stopped as a duo, after thirty years.

They are best known for the Eurovision story of Katinka. Compilations of their records also appeared later, such as Feest met de Spelbrekers.
artiest/de-spelbrekers.listen: Listen to Katinka. Why do you think this song received no points at all at Eurovision in 1962, while it did become a big hit in the Netherlands?

artiest/dead-or-alive.text:
Dead or Alive was an English pop group from Liverpool, centred on the singer Pete Burns. The group grew out of the gothic post-punk band Nightmares in Wax, which Burns gave a new name in 1980. Dead or Alive is important because it delivered the first number 1 hit for the production trio Stock Aitken Waterman, the beginning of the British hit factory of the late 1980s.

Burns worked for years in the Liverpool record shop Probe Records and stood out for his androgynous appearance, which led to frequent comparisons with Boy George. For the single You Spin Me Round (Like a Record) the band worked with Stock Aitken Waterman. The record company Epic saw little in it; Burns, by his own account, borrowed 2,500 pounds to pay for the recording. The single appeared in November 1984 and took seventeen weeks to reach number 1 in England in March 1985. In America it reached number 11. The producers were aiming for Hi-NRG, the fast club music with a pumping bass in eighth notes. Burns himself simply called it disco. The album Youthquake (1985) reached the English top ten.

The sound of You Spin Me Round became a model for other SAW records. In 1986 Bananarama asked for Venus to be made to sound just like it. In Japan the group spent seventeen weeks at number 1 in 1988 with Turn Around and Count 2 Ten. In 2009 Flo Rida used parts of the song in Right Round. Burns died of cardiac arrest in 2016, and with that the group ceased to exist.
artiest/dead-or-alive.listen: In You Spin Me Round (Like a Record) (1984) the synth bass pumps non-stop eighth notes beneath the whole song, at Hi-NRG tempo. Notice how Burns, with his low, theatrical voice, stands on top of that, against the mechanical rhythm.

artiest/dean-parrish.text:
Dean Parrish was an American singer from New York. He was born in 1942 as Philip Anastasi, the child of Italian parents, and grew up in Little Italy. He sang second tenor in a doo-wop group on the street and was a frequent visitor to the Peppermint Lounge, New York's most famous nightclub in the early 1960s. On the advice of Ronnie Spector of The Ronettes he took the name Dean Parrish and began his recording career in 1964.

Between 1964 and 1967 he recorded for four American labels: Laurie, Warner Bros., Musicor and Boom. His soul singles had titles such as I'm On My Way, Tell Her, Determination and Skate. He toured with Dick Clark's Caravan of Stars. In 1967 he took back his old name and became an actor. Musically he remained active as a guitarist, including with Herbie Mann, and as a session musician he played with Jimi Hendrix and Santana in 1970 and with Bob Marley in 1972.

His second life began in England. In the mid-1970s the DJ Russ Winstanley played I'm On My Way at the Wigan Casino, and the song became a Northern soul classic. It was the second-to-last record played at that club's final all-nighter. Parrish himself knew nothing of this for a long time, until in 2001 he contacted Winstanley and performed again for the first time in thirty years. His story shows how a forgotten American single gained a second existence in a British dance hall.
artiest/dean-parrish.listen: Listen to I'm On My Way and notice the tempo and the singing. Why do you think this record works so well on a dance floor?
